---
title: Grade10
summary: One platform behind every storefront, read in one place.
---

Grade10 is one platform wearing several faces. A store, an auction house, a
vault for what a member owns, and the brands that assemble from the same parts
all sit on shared sign-in, shared money handling, and one design system.

This manual explains those parts to a person rather than to a compiler.
Requirements come from the specs, progress from the task lists, visuals from
Figma and the deployed Storybook. The manual points at them and never restates
them, so a page cannot quietly fall out of date with what the platform does.

:::callout{kind="note"}
New here, read [Start here](guides/start-here.md) first. It names the five
minutes each role needs before the rest of this site makes sense.
:::

---
title: Store
summary: The storefront a shopper buys from, and the programme that brings them back.
order: 1
---

The store is the front door. A shopper browses a catalogue, fills a cart,
pays, and is rewarded for coming back. Everything below that sentence is
detail, and every piece of detail lives on its own page.

## What the store owns

The store owns the catalogue, the cart, the checkout, and the loyalty
programme. It does not own identity, money formatting, or the design system —
those are platform concerns, and the store reads them the same way every other
product does.

## What it does not own

Payment capture belongs to the payment provider, and the store never sees a
card number. Sign-in belongs to [shared sign-in](../shared-auth/index.md), and
the store only ever receives a user identity that has already been proved.

---
title: Loyalty
summary: Points a shopper earns on what they spend, and the tiers those points move them through.
spec: grade10-store/loyalty
order: 1
---

A member earns points on qualifying spend, the points expire on a schedule the
programme sets, and what a member has earned over a window decides their tier.
Tier decides the rate they earn at next. That loop is the whole programme.

## How a point comes to exist

A settled sale reaches the programme exactly once, carrying a money amount and
the identity that paid it. The amount is priced into points at the programme's
rate multiplied by the member's tier multiplier, rounded once, and written to
the ledger as a dated credit. Nothing is ever edited afterwards — a balance is
a question asked of the ledger, never a number kept beside it.

### Why the ledger is never edited

An edited row is a row nobody can audit. A claw-back is a new debit that names
the credit it reverses, so the history of a member's balance reads forwards and
reconciles against the money that caused it.

The programme's own money rules follow the platform's
[money amounts](../../platform/money-amounts.md) topic; the product decision
behind the rates lives in the
[loyalty programme PRD](../../../docs/prds/loyalty/programme.md), and the
review that signed it off is in
[spec review](../../../docs/governance/spec-review.md). An older draft at
[tier maths](./tier-maths.md) is gone and this link proves it.

## The ladder Grade10 deploys

| Tier | Earned in 12 months | Multiplier | Expiry | Invitation only | Reward menu | Support queue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bronze | 0 | 1.0x | 12 months | no | standard | standard |
| Silver | 5,000 | 1.25x | 12 months | no | standard | standard |
| Gold | 20,000 | 1.5x | 18 months | no | extended | priority |
| Onyx | not earnable | 2.0x | 24 months | yes | full | concierge |

::spec{id="grade10-store/loyalty"}

:::detail{title="How a balance is derived at an instant" for="engineer"}
A balance is the sum of credits that are unspent and unexpired at the instant
asked about. There is no sweep job: expiry is a comparison against the credit's
own window, evaluated at read time, so a balance read a millisecond after a
credit expires is already correct.

Debits draw on credits oldest-first, and each debit records which credits it
drew from. That record is what makes a reversal able to return each credit
carrying its original expiry rather than a fresh one.
:::

::journeys{id="grade10-store/loyalty"}

::cases{id="grade10-store/loyalty"}

The one scenario people ask about most often, on its own:

::spec{id="grade10-store/loyalty" scenario="grade10-site-loyalty-programme-SC-04"}

Checkout is the surface points are spent on, so what is moving there matters
here too:

::changes{spec="grade10-store/checkout"}

::image{src="assets/loyalty-tiers.png" alt="The four tiers as a ladder, with the earning threshold and multiplier of each" caption="The ladder Grade10 deploys. Onyx sits outside the earning path on purpose."}

---
title: Checkout
summary: Pricing a cart, taking the money, and turning both into an order.
spec: grade10-store/checkout
order: 2
---

Checkout is the shortest path between a filled cart and a settled order, and
the place where the most can go wrong. It is written as a sequence because it
runs as one: each step either completes or the whole attempt is abandoned.

:::flow{title="Placing an order" diagram="assets/checkout-flow.svg"}
## Cart is priced

The cart is priced in one pass: line prices, then promotions, then the
member's point balance if they choose to spend it, then tax and shipping. The
result is a quote with an expiry, and nothing downstream re-prices.

::spec{id="grade10-store/checkout" requirement="A quote is priced once and expires"}

## Payment is authorised

The quote is handed to the payment provider with an idempotency key derived
from the quote id. An authorisation holds the money without capturing it, so a
failure after this point costs the shopper nothing.

## Order is settled

Capture and order creation happen together. The order is the receipt: it
carries the quote it was priced from, the authorisation it was paid by, and the
points it earned. A repeated settle answers with the same order.
:::

:::callout{kind="decision"}
Authorise then capture, rather than a single charge. A single charge is one
fewer call, but it makes every failure after payment a refund instead of a
released hold — and a refund is visible on the shopper's statement.
:::

:::callout{kind="warning"}
A quote that has expired is never silently re-priced. The shopper is shown the
new price and asked again. Re-pricing behind their back is how a checkout
charges more than the screen said.
:::

::figma{url="https://www.figma.com/design/9aXqZ2mQ/Grade10-Store?node-id=412-1180" title="Checkout, mobile"}

::story{id="blocks-store-cart--default" title="Cart block, default state" height="420"}

::spec{id="grade10-store/checkout"}

::cases{id="grade10-store/checkout"}

---
title: Auction
summary: Timed sales where the price is set by the people who want the thing.
order: 2
---

The auction house runs timed sales. A lot opens, bids arrive, the clock runs
down, and the highest bid at the close wins. Everything else — extensions,
proxy bidding, payment holds — exists to make that sentence survive contact
with real bidders.

::children

---
title: Bidding
summary: What a bid is, when it counts, and what stops a sniper from deciding every sale.
spec: grade10-auction/bidding
order: 1
---

A bid is an irrevocable offer at a price, timestamped by the server and never
by the bidder. Two bids at the same price are ordered by arrival, and the
earlier one wins — which is why the server clock is the only clock that counts.

::spec{id="grade10-auction/bidding"}

::journeys{id="grade10-auction/bidding"}

---
title: Stored items
summary: What a member keeps in the vault, and who can ever see it.
order: 1
---

The vault holds what a member has bought and chosen not to take delivery of.
It is a custody record, not a wallet: every item in it has a real thing behind
it, and the record names where that thing physically is.

Nothing here has a spec yet. The product is listed in the manual so the shape
of it is written down before the requirements are.

---
title: Sign-in
summary: One identity across every storefront, proved once.
order: 1
---

Every product reads identity from the same place and none of them store a
password. A member signs in once and is known everywhere the brand reaches.

::children

---
title: Sessions
summary: How long a proved identity stays proved, and what ends it early.
spec: shared-auth/sessions
order: 1
---

A session is a claim that an identity was proved at a moment, carried by a
token with an expiry. It is renewable while it is alive and worthless once it
is not.

::spec{id="shared-auth/sessions"}

---
title: Design system
summary: The controls every console and storefront is built from.
order: 1
---

One set of components, themed per brand. A product picks no brand's colours —
it composes the primitives and lets the app it ships in decide how they look.

::children

---
title: Tokens and themes
summary: Where a colour, a radius, or a spacing value is allowed to be decided.
spec: shared-ui/tokens
order: 1
---

A component never names a colour. It names a token, and a theme decides what
that token is worth. That is the whole rule, and every deviation from it is a
brand leaking into shared code.

::spec{id="shared-ui/tokens"}

::figma{url="https://www.figma.com/design/7bTkL9pR/Grade10-Design-System?node-id=86-3459" title="Button, every variant"}

::story{id="components-forms-button--all-variants" title="Button, every variant"}

---
title: Money amounts
summary: One representation of money, so no product invents a second one.
spec: money-amounts
order: 1
---

Money is an integer of minor units plus a currency code. It is never a float,
never a string at rest, and never a bare number without its currency beside it.

:::detail{title="What a rounding bug actually costs" for="qa"}
A half-cent lost per line on a ten-line order is five cents. Five cents across
a hundred thousand orders a month is five thousand dollars a year that nobody
can account for, and an auditor will find it before finance does.

Rounding happens once, at the last step that produces a number a person sees.
Every intermediate value keeps full precision.
:::

::spec{id="money-amounts"}

---
title: Dates and times
summary: One clock, one representation, and one place a timezone is allowed to matter.
spec: dates-and-times
order: 2
---

Every timestamp is stored in UTC and rendered in the reader's zone. A date
without a zone is a bug, and a date parsed from a string without a format is
two bugs.

The spec below is currently unreadable — the manual mirrors it rather than
hiding the break.

::spec{id="dates-and-times"}

---
title: Start here
summary: Five minutes per role, and what to read after them.
order: 1
---

This manual is read by four different jobs and it does not reorder itself for
any of them. What changes is where you start.

## If you write requirements

Start at a product landing page, read its capability pages top to bottom, and
ignore every collapsed row. The prose above a spec block is the part a person
wrote for you; the rows below it are the machine-checkable version of the same
thing.

## If you build it

Start at the spec block and expand everything. Every requirement row and every
scenario carries a permanent id and a copy-link — paste those into a pull
request instead of quoting the text, because the text can be edited and the id
cannot.

## If you test it

Start at the test cases block. It names which scenarios are traced and, more
usefully, how many are not.

## If you design it

Start at the Figma and Storybook cards. They load on click, so a page full of
them still opens instantly.

:::callout{kind="warning"}
Nothing on this site is the source of truth. The specs, the task lists, and the
Figma files are. If a page here disagrees with them, the page is wrong and the
fix belongs in the page.
:::

---
title: Writing a page
summary: The block grammar, and the two ways a page breaks.
order: 2
---

A page is YAML frontmatter followed by a sequence of blocks. Everything between
directives is markdown; directives sit at column zero and never indent.

## The frontmatter

Four keys, in this order, and no others. An unknown key is a parse error rather
than a silently dropped field, because the editor writes this file back.

~~~yaml
title: Loyalty
summary: Points a shopper earns on what they spend.
spec: grade10-store/loyalty
order: 1
~~~

## Leaves and containers

A leaf is one line. A container opens with three colons and closes with a bare
three colons, and containers never nest.

~~~markdown
::spec{id="grade10-store/loyalty" scenario="grade10-site-loyalty-programme-SC-04"}

:::callout{kind="note"}
One level of body, markdown plus leaf directives.
:::
~~~

## What a broken reference looks like

A reference that does not resolve is never silently blank. This page asks for a
user story that does not exist, on purpose:

::spec{id="grade10-auction/bidding" story="bidding-US-99"}

The same rule holds for links. A relative link out of the manual into the
product briefs resolves to the file on GitHub, a link to another manual page
becomes a route, and [anything else](../../nowhere/at-all.md) is struck through
where it stands.

specs.title: Loyalty
specs.purpose: A points-and-tiers membership programme: members earn points on qualifying spend, points expire, tiers change what a member earns, and points buy items from a reward menu.
specs.featureSet: Membership and ledger, earning and expiry, tiers and invitations, rewards and redemption, operator console, member surface.

requirements.name: One member record per user, created on first activity
requirements.text:
The programme SHALL hold exactly one member record per user identity, created the first time anything is recorded for that user, and SHALL treat joining as a separate act from having activity recorded.

The member record SHALL hold no personal data beyond the user identity. Names, email addresses and every other identity attribute stay in the identity system.

scenarios.name: Activity precedes joining
scenarios.text:
- **WHEN** points are recorded for a user who has never joined
- **THEN** a member record exists and holds those points
- **AND** the member is reported as not joined until they join

scenarios.name: Joining is idempotent
scenarios.text:
- **WHEN** a member joins more than once
- **THEN** the first join date stands and later attempts change nothing

requirements.name: The ledger is the only source of a balance
requirements.text: Every point movement SHALL be recorded as a dated entry that is never edited or deleted. A balance SHALL be derived by asking the ledger, never stored as a running total.

scenarios.name: Balance excludes expired and spent points
scenarios.text:
- **WHEN** a balance is asked for at a given instant
- **THEN** it counts only credits that are unspent and unexpired at that instant

scenarios.name: A balance never goes negative
scenarios.text:
- **WHEN** any debit is recorded
- **THEN** it draws only on credits that have points remaining
- **AND** no sequence of recorded activity can drive a member below zero

scenarios.name: Every debit is fully accounted
scenarios.text:
- **GIVEN** a debit that draws on more than one credit
- **WHEN** the debit is recorded
- **THEN** the sum of what it drew from each credit equals the debit

requirements.name: A tier reached by earning ratchets up
requirements.text: A tier earned over the programme's measurement window SHALL hold even after the points that won it expire. A tier SHALL never fall because a balance fell.

scenarios.name: Earned tier holds after points expire
scenarios.text:
- **GIVEN** a member who reached Gold on points that have since expired
- **WHEN** their tier is evaluated
- **THEN** they are still Gold

scenarios.name: Tier history records each move
scenarios.text:
- **WHEN** a member's tier changes
- **THEN** the move is recorded with its date and the reason that caused it

requirements.name: A redemption keeps the price it was made at
requirements.text: What the member paid SHALL be recorded on the redemption, so repricing a reward never rewrites what an earlier redemption cost.

scenarios.name: Repricing does not rewrite history
scenarios.text:
- **GIVEN** a reward redeemed at 500 points and later repriced to 800
- **WHEN** the earlier redemption is read
- **THEN** it still reads 500

scenarios.name: Stock is not oversold
scenarios.text:
- **WHEN** two redemptions race for the last unit of a stocked reward
- **THEN** exactly one succeeds and the other is refused

scenarios.name: Restored points keep their original expiry
scenarios.text:
- **WHEN** a redemption is reversed
- **THEN** each credit it drew from is restored carrying its own original expiry

journeys.title: Member earns points on qualifying spend
journeys.text:
**As a** member,
**I want** my balance to follow the money I spend and keep spent, priced once at my tier's rate,
**so that** what I can redeem is exactly what my qualifying spend earned.

journeys.title: Member advances through the tier ladder
journeys.text:
**As a** member,
**I want** my tier derived from what I earned and kept when those points expire,
**so that** the rate I earn at reflects the standing I reached rather than what my balance happens to be today.

journeys.title: Member redeems points for a reward
journeys.text:
**As a** member,
**I want** to spend my points at the price the reward carried when I redeemed it,
**so that** a later reprice, a sell-out or a reversal never changes what that redemption cost me.

testCases.title: Membership is created by activity, not by joining
Ledger arithmetic holds under concurrent debits
A repriced reward does not rewrite an earlier redemption

specs.title: Checkout
specs.purpose: Turning a priced cart into a paid order exactly once, with every failure leaving the shopper no worse off than before they started.

requirements.name: A quote is priced once and expires
requirements.text: Pricing SHALL happen in one pass and produce a quote with an expiry. No step after pricing SHALL recompute a price.

scenarios.name: A quote outlives no more than its window
scenarios.text:
- **WHEN** a quote is presented after its expiry
- **THEN** it is refused and the shopper is re-quoted

scenarios.name: A re-quote is shown before it is charged
scenarios.text:
- **GIVEN** an expired quote whose new price is higher
- **WHEN** the shopper continues
- **THEN** the new price is shown and confirmed before any money moves

requirements.name: Payment is authorised before it is captured
requirements.text: The provider SHALL be asked for an authorisation, and capture SHALL happen only as part of settling the order.

scenarios.name: A failure after authorisation releases the hold
scenarios.text:
- **WHEN** settling fails after an authorisation
- **THEN** the hold is released and nothing is captured

requirements.name: Settling is idempotent
requirements.text: A repeated settle for the same quote SHALL answer with the order the first settle created, and SHALL NOT create a second one.

scenarios.name: A repeated settle answers once
scenarios.text:
- **WHEN** settle is called twice for one quote
- **THEN** both calls answer with the same order id

scenarios.name: A retried settle captures once
scenarios.text:
- **WHEN** settle is retried after a network timeout
- **THEN** the provider captures exactly one payment

specs.title: Bidding
specs.purpose: Accepting offers on a lot, ordering them by the server's clock, and closing on the highest one standing.

requirements.name: A bid is timestamped by the server
requirements.text: The server SHALL stamp every bid on arrival. A timestamp supplied by a client SHALL be ignored.

scenarios.name: Two equal bids are ordered by arrival
scenarios.text:
- **WHEN** two bids at the same price arrive
- **THEN** the one the server stamped first stands

requirements.name: A late bid extends the close
requirements.text: A bid inside the extension window SHALL push the close out by the window, so no lot can be decided by arrival timing alone.

scenarios.name: A bid in the last seconds extends the lot
scenarios.text:
- **GIVEN** a lot with ten seconds left and a thirty second extension window
- **WHEN** a bid arrives
- **THEN** the close moves to thirty seconds after that bid

scenarios.name: Extensions do not compound without bids
scenarios.text:
- **WHEN** no further bid arrives inside the window
- **THEN** the lot closes at the extended time and not later

journeys.title: Bidder is not beaten by the clock
journeys.text:
**As a** bidder,
**I want** a late bid to extend the lot,
**so that** winning is a matter of what I will pay rather than how close to the close I clicked.

specs.title: Sessions
specs.purpose: Carrying a proved identity for a bounded time, renewable while alive and worthless once expired.

requirements.name: A session expires on its own
requirements.text: A session SHALL carry an expiry and SHALL stop being accepted at it, with no revocation call required.

scenarios.name: An expired token is refused
scenarios.text:
- **WHEN** a token is presented after its expiry
- **THEN** it is refused and no renewal is offered

requirements.name: A password change ends every session
requirements.text: Changing the secret that proves an identity SHALL invalidate every session created before the change.

scenarios.name: Other devices are signed out
scenarios.text:
- **WHEN** a member changes their password on one device
- **THEN** sessions on every other device stop being accepted

specs.title: Tokens and themes
specs.purpose: Keeping every literal colour, radius and spacing value in a theme, so a component carries no brand.

requirements.name: A component names a token, never a value
requirements.text: A shared component SHALL reference design tokens only. A literal colour, radius or spacing value in shared code SHALL fail review.

scenarios.name: A brand swap changes nothing but the theme
scenarios.text:
- **WHEN** a second brand's theme is applied
- **THEN** every shared component renders in that brand with no component change

specs.title: Money amounts
specs.purpose: One representation of money across every product: an integer of minor units and a currency code.

requirements.name: Money is minor units plus a currency
requirements.text: A money amount SHALL be an integer of minor units together with an ISO currency code. A floating point number SHALL never represent money.

scenarios.name: A bare number is refused
scenarios.text:
- **WHEN** an amount arrives without a currency
- **THEN** it is refused rather than defaulted

scenarios.name: Mixed currencies do not add
scenarios.text:
- **WHEN** two amounts in different currencies are added
- **THEN** the operation is refused

requirements.name: Rounding happens once
requirements.text: Intermediate values SHALL keep full precision. Rounding SHALL happen at the last step producing a number a person sees.

scenarios.name: A split total matches the whole
scenarios.text:
- **WHEN** a total is split across lines and re-added
- **THEN** the sum equals the total exactly

error.message: scenario `dates-SC-04` is declared twice; the second one at line 41 would silently replace the first

changes.title: Rotate session signing keys without signing anyone out
changes.why: A key rotation today invalidates every live session, so it only ever happens during an incident — which is the worst moment to do it.

changes.title: Tiered loyalty
changes.why: A flat earn rate rewards the first order and the hundredth the same, so the programme gives its best customers no reason to stay.

changes.title: Express checkout for a saved payment method
changes.why: A returning shopper re-enters details the store already holds, and abandons at the step that asks for them.

changes.title: Proxy bidding up to a limit
changes.why: Bidders sit on a lot for its final hour because there is no way to say what they would pay without saying it out loud.

changes.title: Edit a manual page in the browser
changes.why: A page nobody can fix in the moment they notice it is wrong stays wrong.
